memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But Jacob said, 'My son will not go down there with you; his brother is dead and he is the only one left. If harm comes to him on the journey you are taking, then you will bring my gray head down to the grave in sorrow.'" - Gen 42:38 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jacob refuses. He will not let Benjamin go: "his brother is dead and he is the only one left." Simeon remains imprisoned in Egypt, the family's grain will run out, yet Jacob clings to Benjamin, unable to bear the thought of another loss. His grief and fear have such a grip on him that he cannot take the step the whole family's survival requires.

We can feel deeply for Jacob. He had suffered real losses, and his fear was born of genuine pain. Yet his fearful clinging was actually endangering everyone — Simeon left in prison, the family facing starvation, all because Jacob could not release his grip on Benjamin. Sometimes our fear, however understandable, holds us back from the very thing God is calling us to do.

There is a hard but freeing truth here. What we cling to most tightly out of fear, we may need to entrust to God. Jacob's white-knuckle grip on Benjamin was born of love, but it was fear-driven, and it kept him stuck. In time, he would have to open his hands — and when he did, he would discover that God had been working salvation all along.

Is there something you are gripping so tightly, out of fear of loss, that it is holding you and others back? Bring that fear to God. Often the very thing we are most afraid to release is the thing God is asking us to entrust to Him. Our treasures are always safest in His hands, not our own clenched fists.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What am I clinging to out of fear that God may be asking me to release?
2. Is my fearful grip holding me or others back from God's path?
3. Can I entrust even my greatest treasure to God's care?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, where fear makes me cling tightly to what I love, help me to open my hands and entrust it to You. My treasures are safest in Your care. Give me courage to release and to trust. Amen.
